study: Original contributions in expanded Physics topics
scope: On-demand 18-subject Physics pilot. The public four-subject edition and the other field ranking configurations are outside this intervention.

calibration.method: Pairs use the same three saved collections and embedding files. All first-stage proposals and their receipts were compared byte for byte. Every paper in each second-stage receipt was checked against its title or abstract offsets. Case judgments distinguish a common physical output from a shared method or discussion of previous work. Codex made the editorial judgments against the cited authors and publishers on November 20.

source_role_examples.assessment: The authors review earlier magnetic flux and atmospheric heating relations. They identify the solar and stellar measurements by their original citations.

source_role_examples.contribution: additional analysis of an earlier calculation
source_role_examples.assessment: The earlier paper already gave the temperature and momentum trend, including separate longitudinal and transverse masses at three fixed temperatures. The conference paper maps both masses over the two-dimensional parameter plane and gives its maximum splitting of about 26 MeV. We count that quantitative extension and treat the underlying calculation as shared with the May paper.

editorial_reviews.headline: Oxygen migration, magnetic contacts and annealing reshape superconducting transport states
editorial_reviews.assessment: The first paper images oxygen redistribution and links it to transport. The second measures magnetic-history-dependent superconductivity. The third resolves voltage kinks at breakdown. Transport is a shared measurement technique, but these three outcomes differ. The English attributes each observation and model to its study.

editorial_reviews.headline: Simulated decoders match or beat BP+OSD logical error rates on surface and qLDPC codes
editorial_reviews.assessment: The simulations compare logical error rates with BP+OSD. The brief correctly identifies simulations and the synthesis distinguishes evaluation cost from hardware timing.

editorial_reviews.headline: Inferred distances: model-dependent Cepheid and M31 results, 6% red clump precision
editorial_reviews.assessment: The common outcome is an inferred stellar or galaxy distance. Agreement in the Cepheid analysis depends on the adopted mass–luminosity relation, 6% is precision in the clean red-clump tier, and the M31 distance depends on the population models.

editorial_reviews.headline: Theory and numerics map transport and current statistics in driven SEP and open XXZ chains
editorial_reviews.assessment: Two papers calculate signed-current statistics. The exclusion-process study maps unsigned dynamical activity. Generalizing the headline to transport still leaves the three without the claimed common current observable.

editorial_reviews.headline: Metasurfaces and a silicon chip select optical skyrmion topology in three device schemes
editorial_reviews.assessment: Each device controls a polarization texture and its topological invariant. The chip study reconstructs the skyrmion number from measured Stokes components. The brief uses the experimental sense of “measured” and the synthesis names that reconstruction.

editorial_reviews.headline: Calculations on HH/LH character in Ge hole qubits: designs for LH ground states and HH–LH mixing
editorial_reviews.assessment: Each theoretical model changes the heavy-hole and light-hole character or mixing in a Ge structure. The numerical estimates are attributed to their calculations.

editorial_reviews.headline: Lens-model-dependent H0 inferred from SN 2025wny time delays: 67–81 km/s/Mpc
editorial_reviews.assessment: The three companion papers measure time delays and infer H0 with a lens model. They use the same supernova. The summary distinguishes the spectroscopic, photometric and adopted lens-model estimates.

editorial_reviews.headline: T→P leakage vs r~1e-3: BICEP3 beam-informed sims, CGEM optics sims, LiteBIRD coupled-systematics sims
editorial_reviews.assessment: The headline and brief identify BICEP3 beam-informed simulations. Its primary measurements supply the beam model, while the leakage residual is simulated. The other instruments’ simulated outcomes are identified separately.

editorial_reviews.headline: Model and SED-inferred dust masses span 1e-8 to 1e3 Msun across RSG winds, LRD analogs, one WC outburst
editorial_reviews.assessment: The three report source-associated dust masses. The opening of the synthesis calls them all dust formed, although the red-dot emission fit includes a potentially pre-existing reservoir.

editorial_reviews.headline: Preprints prove regularized channel Rényi continuity at α=1, yielding strong converses
editorial_reviews.assessment: Four theoretical papers establish continuity of the regularized channel divergence and strong converses under the hypotheses stated for each result.

editorial_reviews.headline: Theory proposals tune cavity photon antibunching via feedback, drive phase or modulation
editorial_reviews.assessment: The feedback cavity, modulated Raman cavity and Kerr dimer each calculate how drive parameters affect photon counting correlations. The English describes model results and identifies the role of each drive.

editorial_reviews.headline: Three model tests of the LZ 248 keV recoil: PBH-boosted DM excluded, dark atom and decay-fed flux viable
editorial_reviews.assessment: All three model the same xenon recoil. The headline calls the decay-fed flux viable, although the authors report a conditional benchmark and explicitly leave a detector-level fit and further constraints open. The exclusion of boosted dark matter is also specific to the calculation tested.

editorial_reviews.headline: Theory: many-body working media set heat-engine work and efficiency, in Potts, Dicke and BCS-BEC models
editorial_reviews.assessment: All three theoretical engine studies evaluate work or efficiency with interacting working media. The synthesis treats the different cycles and material models separately.

editorial_reviews.headline: Effective models place the chiral transition differently in T-μB and T-eB: crossover, shifted CEP, falling Tc
editorial_reviews.assessment: The NJL paper includes a chiral pseudocritical temperature curve in Fig. 1 used to fit its coupling. The authors’ main temperature-decrease result concerns axial symmetry restoration. The headline folds that result into the chiral-transition comparison.

editorial_reviews.headline: Three theoretical quantum-battery charging schemes: antiblockade, waveguide bound-state, cavity-dressed ergotropy
editorial_reviews.assessment: Three models report quantum-battery charging performance. The synthesis distinguishes stored energy, efficiency and extractable work and names the assumptions for the reported gains.

editorial_reviews.headline: Reduced-qubit workflows vs classical references: emulated agreement, a 0.23 kcal/mol dimer gap
editorial_reviews.assessment: All compare electronic energies from quantum-algorithm workflows against classical references. The revised text attributes basis dependence, truncation and emulation or device measurements separately.

editorial_reviews.headline: Theory: rate fluctuations, target correlation time and boundary resetting reshape mean capture times
editorial_reviews.assessment: Mean capture or first-passage time is the common output across all three diffusion models. The English retains the transition, optimum and reset-point condition for their respective models.

editorial_reviews.headline: Entanglement routing vs optimum: heuristic, exact DP/MILP and emulated neutral-atom QUBO give differing results
editorial_reviews.assessment: All three compare entanglement-delivery routes or schedules under fidelity requirements. The text distinguishes exact or heuristic optimization and emulator benchmarks and assigns the optimality gap to small simulated instances.

editorial_reviews.headline: Three SN spectral series span +1 to +167 d, ≤100 d, and plateau phases, with model-based inferences
editorial_reviews.assessment: The spectra cover different phases of three different supernovae. Observation length is a property of the campaigns. The proposed question identifies no common physical measurement or inference. The descriptive English attributes the dates, spectral bands and models correctly.

editorial_reviews.headline: Theory and simulation of time-varying structures for scattering and frequency control
editorial_reviews.assessment: The common result concerns scattering and conversion in time-modulated structures. The summaries give the different theoretical and numerical methods. The narrower authorship statement concerns what the abstracts say about common data or a companion study.

editorial_reviews.headline: Three methods target strong-coupling non-Markovian spin-boson dynamics with distinct costs
editorial_reviews.assessment: Three distinct schemes benchmark spin–boson dynamics beyond weak coupling. The ancilla algorithm is evaluated in classical simulations, as stated in the synthesis.

editorial_reviews.headline: Computed ISCO shifts from Schwarzschild: dyonic NLED model gives shrinkage
editorial_reviews.assessment: All derive the position or shift of an innermost stable circular orbit. The numerical fit and the theoretical perturbation argument remain distinct.

editorial_reviews.headline: U(1) gauge models fit LZ's measured 248 keV recoil, assuming inelastic DM scattering
editorial_reviews.assessment: Independent phenomenological calculations interpret the same measured LZ candidate with distinct gauge models. The English explicitly identifies one event and distinguishes recoil energy from model inference.

editorial_reviews.headline: Model-inferred inelastic DM couplings from the high-energy LZ recoil candidate
editorial_reviews.assessment: The three calculations infer model-dependent inelastic couplings or candidate compositions. The measured LZ candidate is common to this topic and the preceding one and supplies no independent experimental replication.

editorial_reviews.headline: Variational optimizer benchmarks: verdicts shift with censoring, targets and cost pricing
editorial_reviews.assessment: All compare optimizers for variational circuits. The English describes censoring, cost conventions, a null result and the limited information supplied by the hardware runs.

broad_prompt.reviewed_memberships: All 11 newly ranked paper sets and all 14 previously graded paper sets retained by this version. Seven other ranks with pre-existing memberships were outside the previous sample.

targeted_prompt.result: Retained in the pilot. The presentation comment is checked only when venue and abstract both supply relevant cues. The independent result in a conference contribution remains eligible. The previous B-decay rank disappears. The earlier current/activity group is still withdrawn in the reader. The two earlier missed groups still need work.

prior_case_reviews_rechecked.assessment: The works address exactly the same inclusive radiative branching ratio, but Huber's conference proceedings recapitulate previously published calculations. Section 5 explicitly attributes both calculations to earlier work. The other two papers give the technical calculation and its phenomenological analysis. The digest counts the report toward the minimum of three original contributions and assigns it new calculation work. Its exclusive claim about the charged-Higgs bound also fails against equation 17 of the proceedings.

All three benchmark logical decoding error against belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding. The digest identifies code families, noise models and the simulated setting. The neural decoder's 0.2% figure refers to computational complexity. It is kept separate from its decoding accuracy.

The exclusion-process paper counts every hop, including opposing hops. Its conclusion identifies directional current statistics as future work. The quantum generating-function paper tracks transferred charge, and the noisy XXZ paper computes current counting statistics. The digest's headline extends the current result to the exclusion-process analysis.

All three model how light-hole admixture changes electrically driven spin response in germanium qubits. The copy attaches the isotropic response, the Rabi-frequency and coherence trade-off, and the cavity figure of merit to their respective calculations. It identifies the device proposals as theoretical.

All three treat the polarization-resolved in-medium response of the same phi meson. The sum-rule study separates transverse and longitudinal masses. The two spectral models also derive spin alignment and differ on its sensitivity to density. The synthesis correctly limits the spin-alignment ratio to the two holographic calculations.

The three papers estimate source-associated dust mass in solar units. The red-supergiant model predicts wind condensates, the Wolf–Rayet study infers dust formed in an outburst, and the little-red-dot analysis estimates total dust reservoirs. Photometry does not establish how much of those reservoirs formed in the outflow. The synthesis opens by calling all three values dust formed. The systems also differ, so the numbers cannot isolate a measurement-method effect.

The papers all evaluate instrumental temperature-to-polarization contamination in microwave-background measurements. BICEP3 measured its detector beams and used them in timestream simulations to estimate residual leakage. The headline presents the residual itself as measured. CGEM separately observed its beam on the sky, while the LiteBIRD paper simulates coupled instrumental effects.

The three companion papers contribute spectroscopy, photometry and lens modelling of the same supernova. Each provides a distinct original measurement or model. The summary gives their H0 constraints under the named lens assumptions and identifies the shared observations.

One contribution establishes time complexity for forward ordinary-differential-equation evolution. Barthe proves truncation convergence and treats posterior-state preparation. An and colleagues instead test classical parameter recovery from a quantum loss for inverse problems. The latter two share an inverse-problem setting, but all three lack a common output or physical benchmark.

The angle-resolved spectra demonstrate electronic replica bands, ptychography measures layer-resolved atomic relaxation, and the trilayer calculations predict relaxed domains and topological bands. The reconstruction study and simulation share structural observables. The large-angle bilayer experiment attributes its replicas to interlayer scattering and supplies a different observable.

All three studies use TESS light curves to measure pulsation periods or frequencies in delta Scuti stars. The catalogue supplies population period and amplitude distributions and the two high-amplitude samples resolve the modes of individual stars. A comparison can retain the shared authors and TESS provenance and distinguish population evidence from individual mode identifications.

The gadolinium study predicts atomic-ion emission lines. The other two address tetraquark radiative properties and resonance poles. The particles, measured quantities and spectra differ, leaving fewer than three comparable works.

The first group separates ultrafast spin and orbital pumping currents, the second measures interface spin-to-charge conversion, and the third calculates torques exciting particular magnon modes. Sharing a magnetic interface does not supply a single conversion efficiency or magnon yield across the three.

The four preprints tackle the same order-one limit and its consequence for discriminating a pair of quantum channels. The brief's dates are the September 24 and 25 Physics announcements. The synthesis attributes the distinct proof methods and finiteness assumptions to their authors. Zhu and Wang explicitly extend the result to general testers and identify their exponent.

Four groups calculate different endothermic scenarios for the same single LZ recoil. Each contributes a new model calculation. The brief distinguishes the excluded parameter region of the primordial-black-hole model from the other benchmark predictions. The experimental paper confirms the recoil energy and its two reported uncertainties. The gamma-line estimate is conditional on radiative decay.

All three compare black-hole formation scenarios with gravitational-wave observations. The triple-star simulations account for several low-mass population features, the event fits test component-spin priors, and the population model infers channel efficiencies. The digest attributes the comparable channel fractions to the third model and describes mass-ratio reversal as a proposed pathway.

The common physical question is how time variation controls scattering into different frequencies. In the cylinder model the wavevector is conserved even when the direction of energy transport changes. The multilayer design also produces distinct momentum channels. The synthesis says a shared author name is the only stated connection, although the two manuscripts name the same coauthor and department at Aalto University.

The three studies calculate an electronic energy and quantify its agreement with a classical reference. Each numerical value is tied to its system, basis or comparator. The hardware check for the hydrogen chain is an energy difference, distinct from the emulated self-consistent-field energy. The benzene result is the interaction minimum for the stated basis.

All three calculate how controllable parameters affect a quantum battery's energy. The antiblockade enhancement, distance threshold for two emitters, and double-dot ergotropy belong to separate models. The synthesis identifies theory throughout and preserves the distinction between stored energy, charging efficiency and extractable work.

All three analyses infer the Hubble constant with DESI acoustic-distance information. The numerical estimates and named priors agree with the papers. The synthesis calls all three calibrators late-universe or low-redshift probes. The second analysis uses an early-universe baryon-density prior from primordial nucleosynthesis.

All three calculate the innermost stable circular orbit for a perturbed Schwarzschild spacetime. Kazempour and Sun also compare the shadow with Sgr A* data. The Letelier study fits oscillation frequencies under its stated precession model. Hohenegger develops a response expansion for orbital and shadow observables. The copy distinguishes that calculation from the observational fits.

Schuldt and colleagues infer H0 from a lensed supernova using a specified cluster mass model. The other two papers report the same eleven lensed quasars, including the matter-density prior. The English gives the two estimates and uncertainties and correctly identifies the companion publications.

The three groups benchmark optimization of parametrized quantum circuits. Wei compares circuit-evaluation costs, Belozerova tests energy error and success on hydrogen chains, and Cotea evaluates objectives on several workloads. Cotea includes Adam updates and distinguishes hardware case studies from the simulator ranking. The synthesis keeps those conditions attached.

The three theory teams ask whether the same high-energy recoil can be accommodated by their dark-matter candidates, then test different additional constraints. The surviving fractions, solar limits and mass ranges are attributed to the appropriate benchmarks. All three interpret the existing LZ observation.

All three test distinct gauge models against the same LZ event. The quoted recoil energy and maximum local significance agree with the detector collaboration. The account identifies one event and treats subsequent constraints and gravitational-wave signals as model-dependent predictions. Rank 5 also interprets this event with different papers.

Two papers examine transitions between extended and localized single-particle states. The qudit paper instead locates a many-body ergodicity threshold as a function of local Hilbert-space dimension. The network paper measures spreading and Shannon entropy across topologies. The three lack a common localization threshold or transport comparison.

The condensate study reports scaling of single-parameter Fisher information near dynamical saddle points. The trapped-ion proposal evaluates weak-field sensitivity with detuned squeezing and short interrogation. The level-crossing study targets simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters against a Holevo bound. Their sensitivities refer to different tasks and resource measures.

Aditi and Becker construct intervals for state fidelity. Köhne and colleagues estimate circuit fidelity decay versus depth. Porta-San Miguel and colleagues certify whether a logical circuit error rate falls below a threshold. These outputs cannot support one three-study estimate of fidelity or error.

Three teams directly measure stellar rotation periods from cyclic emission. The radio and optical ultracool-dwarf periods agree near 3.079 hours. The KIC red-giant analysis measures a 35.515-day spot period, and the xi Persei team obtains a 2.040514-day period from spectroscopic and photometric variability. The red-giant result is in the primary paper's period analysis. The maser and wind papers need not enter the comparison.

The condensate study predicts bistability in matter-wave transmission, the lattice-clock experiment measures spectroscopic linewidth and coherence time, and the photonic proposal predicts gravitationally induced phase and visibility changes. Interferometry alone supplies no common measured quantity for the three works.

targeted_prompt.source_of_english: All 26 surviving ranks reused identical headline, brief, synthesis and result evidence. The changed synthesis guidance is tested on new material in the independent week. September 30 and October 14 reproduce the prior English HTML byte for byte.

additional_trigger_check.assessment: The submission comment identifies a Physics Reports review written in 2025. The authors give an overview of the MSHT fits, discuss ongoing studies and cite the original fits. This proposal and the separate solar-review proposal were also excluded by the baseline review. Only the radiative-decay proposal changed its ranking eligibility.

independent_edition.sampling: Upper half rounds up. Start at the top for upper and the bottom for lower, taking up to ten from each. For exclusions take the first three wholly rejected detailed proposals and first two wholly rejected initial candidates ordered by SHA-256 of the newline-separated, sorted paper identifiers. Evaluate eligible shared outcomes and all English claims against the source texts. Report the original wording before reader corrections.
independent_edition.source_verification: The independent September inventory predates the ranked edition. All in-scope first-version arXiv titles and abstracts were hashed from archived versions in the official API. Each stored date, first-version URL, title and abstract was matched to that inventory. Journal eligibility and dates were checked against the APS publisher catalogue. The fresh sample uses the verified authors’ abstracts, with full texts and experiment sources cited separately for material distinctions.

case_reviews.headline: Inelastic DM parameters inferred from LZ's single measured 248 keV recoil candidate
case_reviews.question: Inelastic DM models whose benchmark or parameter space is shown to reproduce the LZ 248 keV recoil event
case_reviews.assessment: Seven theory studies interpret the same LZ recoil through distinct inelastic models. The observed energy and background significance agree with the original experiment. The 2.6σ figure is global, and 3.4σ is the largest local value. The English identifies a single measured candidate and attributes the model parameters to the theory papers.

case_reviews.headline: GRASP2018 RCI plus second-order MBPT: claimed CSF reductions, unquantified in abstracts
case_reviews.question: Whether the second-order perturbation + RCI method in GRASP2018 significantly reduces the CSF space in energy-structure calculations. The papers form a series of successive extensions by the same authors (core-valence, then core, core-core, valence-valence), so they are companion studies, not independent replications; the shared byline only establishes a name match. Each paper applies it to a different ion (Cl III, Fe XV, Fe XV, Se III) and none gives quantitative reduction figures in the abstract.
case_reviews.assessment: The same three authors extend the atomic-structure method to successively different correlation terms. Two calculations use Fe XV. The text identifies the sequence, the ions and the absence of numerical reduction factors in the four abstracts. Each contribution adds a distinct treatment.

case_reviews.headline: Theory tests higher-order effective Hamiltonians for periodically driven quantum systems
case_reviews.question: Accuracy and validity of effective Hamiltonians from high-order Floquet/high-frequency expansions for driven systems
case_reviews.assessment: All three test corrections to effective Hamiltonians for driven systems. The NMR calculation compares expansion methods, the intense-light model benchmarks against Floquet calculations, and the Rydberg analysis derives the effect of higher orders on magnetization and trimers. The summaries distinguish their methods and identify the experimental reach as an estimate.

case_reviews.headline: Theory: nonreciprocity, scars and bound states protect quantum battery energy
case_reviews.question: Strategies that maximize stored and extractable battery energy under dissipative, decoherent or nonreciprocal conditions (stored energy/ergotropy outcome of each protocol)
case_reviews.assessment: Each model gives the stored or extractable energy of an open quantum battery. The steady-state energy ratio, scar-supported work and oscillations with two bound states are attributed to the corresponding calculation.

case_reviews.headline: Theory papers map how modification parameters shift photon spheres and shadow sizes
case_reviews.question: Dependence of photon-sphere radius and critical impact parameter (shadow or capture size) on modification parameters relative to the GR or Schwarzschild limit
case_reviews.assessment: All three compute unstable null-orbit quantities or the critical impact parameter in deformed spacetimes. The black-bounce paper distinguishes the matter parameter’s direct effect on the shadow from the bounce-dependent existence condition. The summaries distinguish computations, proposed tests and constraints from existing weak-field data.

case_reviews.headline: Code performance under leakage, biased, crosstalk and GAD noise: three differing scaling results
case_reviews.question: Logical performance of codes under noise that is not simple independent Pauli noise: leakage, biased and crosstalk noise, and generalized amplitude damping. Each paper reports how logical performance scales with physical noise strength.
case_reviews.assessment: The studies investigate logical performance under different physical error processes. The short summary calls all of them non-Pauli noise. The ZX and ZY study explicitly simulates biased Pauli-X noise with and without correlated XX errors. The other two papers study leakage and generalized amplitude damping.
case_reviews.reader_correction: The three models use different noise channels. The ZX and ZY surface-code study varies the bias of Pauli-X errors and adds correlated XX crosstalk in a separate set of simulations. The honeycomb Floquet study models leakage. The five-qubit study evaluates generalized amplitude damping with post-selected recovery. [Noise models in Table 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.10876v1#S3.T1) · [Leakage simulations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10666v1) · [Damping model](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15924v1)

case_reviews.headline: Model-dependent predictions for the 248 keV LZ xenon recoil from endothermic dark matter
case_reviews.question: Predictions of endothermic dark matter for the 248 keV LZ xenon recoil candidate: how the energy scale, rates and target dependence of the xenon signal follow from the splitting, mass and halo
case_reviews.assessment: The three papers calculate endothermic xenon recoil predictions, one alongside an elastic explanation. The measured energy and detector response enter these comparisons. In the solar study the predicted annihilation rate is tested against an IceCube proxy, while an independent NA64 accelerator limit constrains the benchmark’s mediator parameters. The synthesis describes solar evolution as lying below both limits.
case_reviews.reader_correction: All three calculations use the energy of the reported LZ candidate. In the solar study, the predicted annihilation rate is compared with a model-specific IceCube neutrino constraint. NA64 provides a separate accelerator constraint on the benchmark’s mediator parameters. The authors predict 0.958 accepted LZ events using a reconstructed detector response. [Solar analysis and accelerator constraint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10636v1) · [LZ measurement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.02823v1)

case_reviews.headline: Theory: vortex soliton stability in C_n photonic structures depends on geometry, charge and model
case_reviews.question: Stability of vortex solitons in nonlinear photonic structures with discrete rotational symmetry (C_n) as a function of symmetry and topological charge
case_reviews.assessment: All three calculate the stability of vortex solitons subject to a discrete rotational geometry. The English identifies the fractal/configuration comparison, star-network charge dependence and square droplets, including which charges were examined.

case_reviews.headline: Derived reduced 2D models for deep-water waves over background flows; checks are analytic or numerical
case_reviews.question: Derivation of reduced 2D equations for deep-water surface waves over background flows, with a reported illustration or validation of the reduced model
case_reviews.assessment: The three papers derive reduced surface-wave equations. Gallet explicitly builds Part II on Part I with Tlili. Part II couples the two-dimensional wave amplitude to a three-dimensional background flow and analytically checks conservation. The short summary’s claim of no test and the synthesis’s name-only qualification obscure these facts.
case_reviews.reader_correction: Basile Gallet explicitly builds Part II on the equations he derived with Alexandre Tlili in Part I. The reduced surface-wave amplitude depends on two horizontal coordinates and couples to a three-dimensional background flow. Part II verifies conservation of wave action, energy and horizontal momentum for the inviscid model. The paper leaves numerical studies for future work. [Part I](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11587v1) · [Coupled model](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.11631v1#S2) · [Conservation checks](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.11631v1#S3)

case_reviews.headline: Copy-count bounds for learning low-rank, stabilizer and sparse states, each in its own model
case_reviews.question: Sample complexity bounds for learning/tomography of structured or restricted quantum states, expressed as copies needed versus state parameters and accuracy
case_reviews.assessment: All three give the number of copies required for quantum-state learning under different assumptions. The sparse mixed-state paper already proves a polynomial running-time bound in Theorem 1.2. The open question concerns a near-optimal running time, which the final sentence describes too broadly.
case_reviews.reader_note_anchor: Its time complexity for r>1 remains open
case_reviews.reader_correction: Theorem 1.2 gives an algorithm for sparse mixed states of rank above one with polynomial running time in the number of copies and qubits. The open question is whether a faster algorithm can approach the time needed to read those copies. The authors give nearly optimal copy complexity for mixed states and nearly optimal copy and time bounds for pure states. [Theorem 1.2 and the open question](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.12219v1#S1)

case_reviews.headline: Unmodelled lensing systematics bias S8/σ8, Ωm in simulated Stage-IV analyses; only one gives numbers
case_reviews.question: Size of cosmological-parameter bias (S8/sigma_8, Omega_m) in Stage-IV/LSST-like analyses from an unmodelled astrophysical or observational systematic
case_reviews.assessment: All three forecast biases in cosmological parameters. The headline and brief claim numerical values occur in only one study. The alignment study reports biases up to about 12σ in some simulated survey configurations. The blending study also quantifies cosmological tension and how it changes with its overlap definition.
case_reviews.reader_correction: All three studies quantify effects in simulations. The redshift-distribution study finds shifts of −1.7σ in σ8 and +1.4σ in Ωm for one LSST-like setup. The intrinsic-alignment paper reports biases up to about 12σ in some 15,000-square-degree simulations. The blending paper finds that changing the definition of overlap reduces the tension between two parameter contours from 1.6σ to 0.54σ. The studies use different survey assumptions and comparisons. [Redshift distributions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15542v1) · [Intrinsic-alignment discussion](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.12038v1#S5) · [Blending comparison](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.12158v1#S4.SS5.SSS4)

case_reviews.headline: Local and group SN Ia environments: x1 tracks local age, cousins show lower scatter, local differs from global
case_reviews.question: Does SN Ia environment beyond global host properties (local site or group scale) carry distinct information relevant to SN properties or distance scatter?
case_reviews.assessment: The first paper links local age to supernova light-curve shape. The second measures distance scatter for supernovae in common galaxy groups. The third compares local and global host properties and expressly defers correlations with supernova light curves to another paper. The English gives the individual descriptive results correctly, but these papers supply three different outcomes.
case_reviews.reader_withdrawal: One study relates local stellar age to supernova light-curve shape. A second measures distance scatter for supernovae in the same galaxy group. The third compares the environments at explosion sites with host-galaxy averages and reserves correlations with supernova light curves for a later paper. The three studies do not report a common supernova outcome.

case_reviews.assessment: The three studies directly address the speed and accuracy trade-off of modified quantum decoders relative to a baseline. The A* hybrid retains the original logical error rate while expanding fewer nodes. Parallel sparse blossom proves the same correction for identical input. Early-start clustering reports a modest accuracy loss and less post-measurement idling. Expanded nodes, theoretical parallel time and idling are different cost measures and cannot support a pooled speedup.

Two studies test existence or construction of rotating charged solutions with restrictions on the electromagnetic field. The scalar and anisotropic-matter paper derives static spherical solutions and a duality map. It offers horizon and orbital calculations as later applications. The general goal of deriving a charged metric does not identify one rotation, horizon or field-response result across the three.

The Gaussian-process and recurrent-network studies share mass predictions. The quantum convolution study instead predicts charge radii along isotope chains. These works do not provide a three-paper mass or radius comparison.

The semi-visible-jet paper and DIS paper both report jet transverse momentum under changes in shower matching. The Higgs decay study explicitly applies no jet reconstruction and compares parton-level quantities. Its bottom-quark transverse-momentum plot compares EFT operators at fixed matching accuracy. The feebly coupled particle analysis instead compares hadronic decay multiplicities after selection. The generator technique alone does not supply the third jet measurement.

At least three papers use heat-capacity signs or inequalities to determine local thermodynamic stability of black-hole branches. The quantum Oppenheimer–Snyder analysis finds positive- and negative-capacity branches at fixed quantum parameter. The Gauss–Bonnet analysis approaches a zero-capacity endpoint from the unstable side. The superentropic study tests constant-pressure and constant-volume heat capacities. The ensembles and solution families must be identified. The separate winding-number classification can be left out.
